description: Start here. Loaded datasets (id, name, path, loader config; live streams carry stream), the stream sources start_stream can start, time range, current time, your agent id and tabs, whether PlotJuggler has the user's focus and any dialog the user has open.
name: get_status

description: Load a data file (MCAP, CSV, ULog, Parquet...). Returns when the import has finished (a client tool timeout does not stop it: get_status shows the dataset once it lands). By default the loader's own defaults apply (e.g. every topic). ask_user=true opens PlotJuggler's loader dialog so the user picks topics/options; the call returns when they finish or cancel. config: loader settings JSON (get_status shows the config each loaded dataset used, as a template).
name: open_file

description: Remove a loaded dataset and its data. If derived series depend on it, the user is asked to confirm in PlotJuggler and the call returns their answer.
name: unload_file

description: Reload a dataset from its file with the same loader settings (e.g. after it changed).
name: reload_file

description: Start a live streaming source (get_status lists stream_sources; about says what each one is). By default it uses the settings the user last confirmed in that source's dialog; config passes your own (get_status shows a live stream's config, as a template); ask_user=true opens the source's dialog so the user sets it up, and the call returns when they finish or cancel. Topics appear as the source advertises them.
name: start_stream

description: Stop a live stream; its data stays loaded. dataset: a live stream from get_status.
name: stop_stream

description: Create your own derived series with a Luau or Python script. Python: first line '# pj-script: python', one top-level class T (its id is set for you), @staticmethod create(params) returning T(), and calculate(self, time, value, *more_inputs); imports limited to math, cmath, statistics. A Luau script returns a class: return { name="X", create = function(params) local s = {}; return { calculate = function(t, v) ... return y end } end } (the id is set for you). t is seconds, v the input; keep state in the instance (integrators, bias removal). Several inputs are joined on equal timestamps (fields of one message always are; inputs that share none are refused): calculate(t, v, v1, v2, ...). Several outputs: pass `outputs` [names] and return that many numbers; they become topics <name>/<output>. Listed under Custom Topics, saved in layouts, untouched by the user's undo; the same name replaces it. Returns each output topic with its fields.

inputs.description: series paths as read_series takes them: topic/field, a unique suffix, or dataset:topic/field

name: add_script_series

description: Create a derived series by applying a built-in filter (integral, derivative, absolute, scale, moving_average, moving_rms, moving_variance, outlier_removal, binary_filter, samples_counter, time_since_previous) to one series; params override the filter's defaults. Output name defaults to <input>[filter]. Like add_script_series: listed under Custom Topics, removable with remove_script_series, outside the user's undo. Returns the output topic and field to plot.

input.description: series path, as read_series takes it

name: add_filter

description: Delete a series made with add_script_series or add_filter. Refused while someone else's series (the user's, a plugin's) is built on it, since that would be deleted too.
name: remove_script_series

description: PNG of the PlotJuggler window, including GPU-rendered plots and 3D views, and any dialog the user has open. tab: one of your plot_tab/scene_view tabs to bring to the front first.
name: screenshot

description: Search the loaded topics by substring. If the conversation already lists the loaded topics, use that and call this only for what the listing does not show (it was truncated, or the data changed); otherwise call it to find what is loaded. Optional 'filter' and 'limit'.

dataset.description: only topics from this dataset (substring); useful when several are loaded

filter.description: case-sensitive substring to match topic names

limit.description: max topics to return (default 100, capped at 500)

name: list_topics

description: List the fields of one topic, with types and full paths. Not needed for a topic whose fields the conversation already lists — do not use it to confirm a path you can already see.

topic.description: exact topic name; "dataset:topic" picks one dataset

name: describe_topic

description:
Read summary statistics ('stats'), a min/max-preserving downsample ('buckets'), or up to 200 raw samples inside a mandatory window ('raw'). Non-finite values are 'invalid', excluded from min/max/mean/stddev. buckets are columnar (t0, dt, n, min, max, mean; t_i = t0 + i*dt, or 't' when irregular). Stats carry 't_start_display_s' when playback is bound, so bucket i's display time = t_start_display_s + t0 + i*dt.
'paths' is an ARRAY: ask several at once. A bad path returns as an error beside the ones that worked. A topic path (no field) reads all its numeric fields. buckets take up to 8 paths; raw takes 4. t_start_s/t_end_s (display axis) narrow the read and re-base t; raw REQUIRES both.

paths.description: topic/field paths; a bare string is accepted for a single series

name: read_series

description: Run a Luau computation and get the answer back — nothing is created or shown. Picked automatically: SCALAR (default) takes the same inputs/expression/body/global as create_derived_series and returns stats, add 'buckets' for the shape. OBJECT form kicks in when an input is an object topic or 'at_s'/'window' is given: requires 'body' (reads inputs["<topic>"], returns a table of 'outputs') and 'outputs' (["name:type", …], type is 'number', 'string', or a builtin object type e.g. 'kPointCloud'); 'at_s' evaluates at one display-seconds instant, 'window':{start_s,end_s} over a span, neither defaults to the playhead. Objects come back only as summaries, never bytes. To keep a result, create_derived_object.

body.description: scalar: return ...; object: reads inputs[..], returns table

name: evaluate

description: Create a new derived timeseries computed live from one or more inputs. Each sample sees 'value' (first input), 'v1'..'vN' (further inputs, in order), and 'time' (seconds). Use 'expression' for a stateless formula (e.g. 'value * 2'); for stateful transforms like a derivative, use 'global' (runs once, persistent locals) + 'body' (statements ending in return; return nothing to suppress a sample). Saved in layouts. Undo protection is verified when supported; failure is reported.

body.description: full Luau statements ending in return (overrides expression)

global.description: Luau run once per instance; locals persist across samples

outputs.description: OPTIONAL — several series from ONE node (default: just 'name'). The body then returns one value per output, in order: outputs ['roll','pitch','yaw'] with a body ending 'return r, p, y'. Prefer this over three nodes recomputing the same intermediate.

name: create_derived_series

description: Install a live on-demand computation over object topics (point clouds, scene entities...) — evaluated on request, not eagerly per sample like create_derived_series. 'body' reads inputs["<topic>"] and returns a table of the declared 'outputs' (["name:type", …]). Without 'pin_at_s' it stays live for a later consumer (e.g. scene_view) to query; with 'pin_at_s' it is a FINDING, evaluated once at that display-seconds instant and kept (shown under <plugin>/<name>/…). Either way this call also evaluates it once itself and returns that first bundle. Saved in layouts. Undo protection is verified when supported; failure is reported.

pin_at_s.description: OPTIONAL — pin as a finding, display seconds

name: create_derived_object

description:
Create plot markers from a Luau rule you write (preferred), or from a simple threshold template. There is ONE marker set of yours: calling this again REPLACES it (use remove_markers to clear it). Saved in layouts. Undo protection is verified when supported; failure is reported.
A condition true over a STRETCH of time wants ONE region per stretch (startMarker/closeMarker), never one line per matching sample. The call reports how many markers it produced and of which kind: past ~50, the shape is wrong — merge contiguous hits into regions or raise the threshold.
A per-sample threshold on a raw high-rate signal (IMU and the like) marks vibration, not events: require the condition to hold for a minimum duration and cross-check against an independent slower signal before labeling.
RAW FORM: 'inputs' (series the rule reads) + 'rule' (a whole Luau script, run once over the full series) + optional 'output' (series path the markers attach to; default = first input; "__global__" renders on every plot — only for events meaningful against ANY signal).
Rule vocabulary:
- series("topic/field") -> accessor or nil: s:size(); s:at(i) 0-based -> {t, v} or nil; s:atTime(t) -> interpolated value. GetSeriesNames() -> declared input names. Timestamps t are int64 NANOSECONDS.
- startMarker(t) then closeMarker(t2, opts) -> ONE shaded region per pair.
- createVerticalMarker(t, opts); createPointMarker(t, y, opts); createHorizontalMarker(y, opts); createBandMarker(y_low, y_high, opts); createMarker(x?, y?, opts).
- bandPower(s, f_lo_hz, f_hi_hz) -> summed FFT power for spectral rules.
- opts (all optional): label, description, category, color "#RRGGBB", severity ("info"|"warning"|"error"|"critical"), status.
TEMPLATE FORM (simple threshold): 'series' + 'comparison' (>, <, >=, <=) + 'threshold' + optional 'label' and 'style' ("region" default: one band per exceedance stretch; "line": one vertical line per matching sample).

inputs.description: topic/field paths the rule reads (raw form)

output.description: series path the marker set renders on, or "__global__" (raw form, optional; default = first input)

name: create_markers

description: Remove your marker set from all plots. Only affects markers you created; cannot delete user data.
name: remove_markers

description: List the derived series and marker sets YOU have created in this session. Use it to find the name to remove. A name that is already taken is refused by create_derived_series itself, so there is no need to call this first.
name: list_created

description: Delete a derived series or object you created, by its name. Only your own creations — loaded data cannot be touched. Use it to withdraw a series or object that turned out wrong instead of leaving it in the user's panel. Refused while someone else's series is built on it.
name: remove_derived_series

description: Drive the transport: the time cursor, shared by every plot. action: 'state' (read it), 'play', 'pause', 'seek' (to 'time_s'), 'rate' (to 'rate'; 1.0 = real time, clamped to [0.05, 20]). Every call returns the whole state - playing, current_time_s, range {min_s, max_s}, rate - so a clamped seek shows where the cursor actually landed. Times are DISPLAY-AXIS SECONDS, the numbers on the plot X axes: a feature found in read_series buckets sits at stats.t_start_display_s + bucket.t.
name: playback

description:
Compose plot tabs of your own. A tab you create is marked with your ownership badge and is the only place you may draw: the user's tabs are not yours to fill, zoom or close, and they do not go away when you close yours. Supporting hosts save your tabs with the layout and exclude them from undo/redo; older hosts may keep them only for the session.
action: 'create' (optional 'tab' name and 'title') | 'add'/'remove' ('curves', topic/field paths) | 'zoom' ('start_s'..'end_s' display-axis seconds; omit both to fit) | 'close' | 'list'. Every action answers with the tab as the host holds it, so a curve that did not land shows as missing instead of being reported as drawn. A series you made with create_derived_series is addressable here as 'name/value'.

title.description: tab title shown to the user (create)

name: plot_tab

description:
Open 3D/2D scene views of your own (the scene tabs of pj.plot_tabs.v1), the counterpart of plot_tab: same watermark and ownership, the user's scene docks unreachable.
action: 'create' (optional 'view', 'kind' "3d"|"2d" default "3d", 'title') | 'attach'/'detach' ('topics', object-topic paths) | 'focus' | 'close' | 'list'. Every action reads back what the view actually holds, so a topic that did not land shows as missing instead of attached.

title.description: view title shown to the user (create)

name: scene_view

description: Counts of loaded sources/topics/fields. Only when the user asks for an overview — not as an opening step: list_topics, or a listing already in the conversation, covers that.
name: report_status
